feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Prominent Hong Kong activist pleads guilty to colluding with foreign interests
entry.summary: A prominent Hong Kong democracy activist, Joshua Wong, has pleaded guilty to a charge of colluding with foreign interests under a Beijing-imposed national security law.

entry.title: Alex Ullom's sensibilities were shaped online. In his movie 'It Ends,' you can tell
entry.summary: In the new movie It Ends, four twentysomethings find themselves stuck on an endless road — literally. Filmmaker Alex Ullom says his sensibilities were shaped by growing up online.

entry.title: Secretly moving Raja Shehadeh's diaries from Israeli-occupied West Bank to Scotland
entry.summary: A leading Palestinian writer has secretly moved his archives from the Israeli-occupied West Bank to Scotland, to save it from the risk of destruction in Israeli military operations.

entry.title: A Korean pastor has attracted attention from the Trump administration
entry.summary: South Korea's government is trying to keep religious groups from interfering in politics. The case of one Korean pastor has attracted attention at the highest levels of the U.S. government.

entry.title: Supreme Court arguments can drag on. Chief Justice Roberts is considering some change
entry.summary: Chief Justice John Roberts says he's thinking about how to dial back extra-long oral arguments at the Supreme Court.

entry.title: How AI is being used to track art stolen by the Nazis
entry.summary: As momentum builds to recover artworks stolen during World War Two by the Nazis, researchers have created an AI chatbot that aims to trace the ownership and location history of works of art.

entry.title: Chevron's expansion in Venezuela has implications for the oil industry and the planet
entry.summary: Chevron is expanding its current operations in Venezuela. The deal expands the company's footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty in Venezuela.

entry.title: How do you take care of parents who may not have taken great care of you?
entry.summary: NPR's "It's Been a Minute" podcast explores the complexities of adults who wind up having to care for aging parents with whom they may have had a fraught or even abusive child relationship.

entry.title: Remembering Pierre Damas Bel, an Ohio college student with great promise
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Pastor Carl Ruby of Central Chistian Church in Springfield, Ohio about the death of 20-year-old Pierre Damas Bel, who died after being struck by a truck on the interstate.

entry.title: What's up with the bond market?
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with economist Justin Wolfers of the University of Michigan about what's going on with the bond market — and why it matters to everyday people.
